This document looks at a bunch of DDOT data that's super cool but a little buried on their website. We'll do 3 things:

* DDOT conducts evaluations of their bus priority and bike infrastructure projects. We'll look at those evaluations and try to replicate them.
* We'll also try to scale those evaluations to a bunch of other project that aren't on DDOT's evaluations page, using the same crash data.
* Finally, we'll look at some neat data DDOT staff collect by standing on streets and watching people bike by.


To view the code in this document, click the "show" buttons on the right. Some of this analysis also uses supporting functions I put in a separate set of files; you can find all of the code here: https://github.com/pete-rodrigue/ddot-project-evals

## DDOT's bus and bike project evaluations

First let's look at some of the results from DDOT's detailed before-after analyses of their projects:

<br>

```{r plot_ddot_eval_data}
to_plot <-
  df %>%
  filter(Outcome %in% c("Any Injury", "All Crashes")) %>%
  mutate(Change = Change*-1)

ggplot(to_plot) +
  geom_bar(aes(x=`Project short name`, y=Change, fill=Outcome), stat="identity", position="dodge") +
  labs(y="% decrease in crashes", x="") +
  ggtitle("All projects saw decreases in crashes") +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept=mean(Change[Outcome == "All Crashes"], na.rm=T)), 
             color="#F8766D", linetype="dashed", linewidth=.8, alpha=.5) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept=mean(Change[Outcome == "Any Injury"], na.rm=T)), 
             color="#00BFC4", linetype="dashed", linewidth=.8, alpha=.5) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.title = element_blank())

to_plot <-
  df %>%
  filter(Outcome %in% c("Pedestrian Injury")) %>%
  mutate(Change = Change*-1)

ggplot(to_plot) +
  geom_bar(aes(x=`Project short name`, y=Change), stat="identity", fill="seagreen") +
  labs(y="% decrease in crashes", x="") +
  ggtitle("Pedestrian crashes fell after project completion, sometimes to zero") +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept=mean(Change, na.rm=T)), color="grey", linetype="dashed", size=1) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.title = element_blank())

to_plot <-
  df %>%
  filter(str_detect(Outcome, "Private motor vehicle")) %>%
  group_by(`Project short name`, Outcome) %>%
  summarize(change = mean(Change, na.rm=T)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(Outcome = ifelse(Outcome == "Private motor vehicle AM peak travel time (seconds)", 
                          "AM traffic travel time",
                          "PM traffic travel time"))

ggplot(to_plot) +
  geom_point(
    aes(x=change, color=Outcome, y=`Project short name`), size=3, alpha=.7
  ) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=0), color="black") +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=mean(change[Outcome == "AM traffic travel time"], na.rm=T)), color="#F8766D", linetype="dashed") +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=mean(change[Outcome == "PM traffic travel time"], na.rm=T)), color="#00BFC4", linetype="dashed") +
  labs(x="Change in travel time in seconds", y="") +
  theme_minimal() +
  xlim(c(min(to_plot$change)-10, max(to_plot$change)+25)) +
  theme(legend.title = element_blank()) +
  ggtitle("Drivers' travel times faster on average after project completion")

rm(to_plot); rm(url)
```


```{r }
outcome_vars <-
  c("All Crashes", "Vehicle Crashes", "Bike Crashes", "Pedestrian Crashes", 
    "Any Injury", "Driver Injury", "Bicyclist Injury", "Pedestrian Injury",
    "Driver Serious Injury", "Bicyclist Serious Injury", "Pedestrian Serious Injury")


# load crash data:
cd <- load_crash_data()
# crash_details <- read_csv("data/Crash_Details_Table.csv", show_col_types = F)
# load project shapefiles:
ddot_projs <- 
  st_read("data/ddot-evaluated-projects.geojson", quiet=T) |>
  st_transform(4326) |>
  filter(project_name != "Minnesota Ave Bike Lane Project")

get_crashes_in_corridors <- function(line_sf, crashes_sf, buffer_in_meters) {
  mybuffer <-
    line_sf |>
    st_transform(6487) |>               # EPSG:6487 — NAD83 / Maryland (metres)
    st_buffer(dist = buffer_in_meters,  # X m buffer
              endCapStyle = "FLAT"
              ) |>  
    st_transform(st_crs(ddot_projs))    # reproject back to match cd's CRS
  
  crashes_near_projects <- st_join(crashes_sf, mybuffer, join = st_within, left = FALSE)
  
  crashes_near_projects
}

group_corridor_crashes_by_month <- function(df, group_by_vars = NA, outcome_vars) {
    df                                      |>
    st_drop_geometry()                      |>
    group_by(across(all_of(group_by_vars))) |>
    summarize(
      `All Crashes` = n(),
      across(all_of(outcome_vars), \(x) sum(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
      .groups = "drop_last"
      )                                     |>
    ungroup()
}

crashes_near_projects <- get_crashes_in_corridors(line_sf = ddot_projs, crashes_sf = cd, buffer_in_meters = 4)

cd_in_projs_summed <- 
  group_corridor_crashes_by_month(df = crashes_near_projects, 
                                  group_by_vars = c("project_name", "month", "year", "date"),
                                  outcome_vars = outcome_vars)



```

Below is a quick look at all of the crashes in these project corridors. Note that DDOT seems to map all of these crashes to the roadway center line. I just drew the corridor center lines by hand in Felt GIS, and then made a little buffer aroud each center line in R. I assigned all of the crashes that fell within that buffer to the corridor. 

```{r}
plot_leaflet(
  lines_sf = ddot_projs,

  )
```

## Replicating DDOT project evaluations {.tabset}

Below, we try to replicate those results. The line charts are smoothed, showing a 4 month moving average. The data actually agrees pretty well! This is good, given I only had DDOT's PDF that briefly describes their methodology, not their actual code or a detailed how-to. This suggests the results are relatively robust to little choices about how to do the analysis.

Crashes go down, sometimes by quite a lot, after these projects get installed. 

```{r results="asis"}
for (proj in unique(cd_in_projs_summed$project_name)) {  
  
  if(proj=="15th St NW/SW Protected Bike Lane") {next}
  
  cat("\n### ", proj, "\n") # tab headers
  
  periods <- proj_dates[[proj]]
  p1      <- periods$period_1
  p2      <- periods$period_2
  
  rvs <- plot_crashes_over_time(
    data             = filter(cd_in_projs_summed, year >= 2016 &
                              project_name == proj),      
    smoothing_factor = 4,
    period_1         = p1,
    period_2         = p2,
    title            = proj
  )
  
  print(rvs[[1]])
  cat("\n")
  print(
    rvs[[3]] %>% 
      dplyr::left_join(select(df, `Project name`, Outcome, Change) %>% filter(`Project name` == proj), by=c("series"="Outcome")) %>%
      rename(pct_change_ddot = Change) %>%
      select(-`Project name`) %>%
      knitr::kable()
    )
  
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

## Using additional data to expand on DDOT project evaluations 

DDOT has looked at a few projects in depth. But we can also use DC's crash data to look at every (or almost every) protected and buffered bike lane in DDOT's "bike lane" shapefile that was built in the late 2010s and early 2020s.

Quick methodology:

* Took the ["Bicycle Lanes" shape file](https://opendata.dc.gov/datasets/DCGIS::bicycle-lanes/about) from Open Data DC and subset it to just "protected", "dual protected", "buffered", and "dual buffered" bike lanes. We don't really care about painted bike lanes, since those don't have super robust safety benefits.
* Unioned together all of the subblock segments in that data set by route and build year, since different pieces of some routes were built in different years. I hand-labeled when each piece of the bike lanes were installed by using satellite imagery and google street view (this was a pain). You can find my hand-labeled data set [here](https://felt.com/map/protected-and-buffered-bike-lanes-4U8sjcFHQFif4Pft9CCwicC?loc=38.92185,-76.98843,13.59z).
* Then I overlay the crash data, and assign any crash that's within 4 meters of the roadway segment's center line to the corridor (DDOT codes the crashes to the center line, rather than wherever the MPD officer poked at the map on this iPad). 
* Finally, we just plot the number of crashes per month on each route, before and after the protected or buffered bike lane was installed. I'm only showing routes that have at least 8 subblock segments and were installed between 2017 and 2024. I'm also not showing the lanes we just looked at above!


Here's a quick map of the routes. Hover over each route to see the route name, the install year, and whether it's coded as protected (1) or buffered (0) in the Open Data DC data. 


```{r analysis_globals, fig.width=12}
# which years to include in the analysis
ANALYSIS_YEARS = c(2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2024, 2025)
POST_YEARS     = c(2024, 2025)
# whether to analyze the data at the subblock level (SUBBLOCKKEY) or 
# block level (BLOCKKEY):
ANALYSIS_LEVEL = "SUBBLOCKKEY"
# which treatment groups to include, options include
# switcher     : units that got PBLs between 2020 and 2023 inclusive 
# never_taker  : units that never got PBLs
# late_taker   : units that got PBLs in 2024 or 2025
# always_taker : units that got PBLs before 2019
TREATMENT_GROUPS_TO_INCLUDE = c("switcher", "never_taker")
# whether to include buffered bike lanes as well or just fully protected bike lanes
PBLS_ONLY = FALSE
# a bbox for map plotting so we don't plot tons of data at once:
PLOT_BBOX = c(xmin = -77.015, ymin = 38.94, xmax = -77.010, ymax = 38.944)

# load data:
cd                <- load_crash_data()
pbl               <- load_pbl_data(PBLS_ONLY) 
cabi_sf           <- load_cabi_data()[[1]]
annual_cabi_rides <- load_cabi_data()[[2]]
rs                <- load_subblocks()

pbl_unioned <- pbl                                     |>
  mutate(
    ROUTENAME = if_else(ROUTENAME == "Ramp-36001642", "IRVING ST NW", ROUTENAME),
    ROUTENAME = if_else(ROUTENAME == "KENYON ST NW" , "IRVING ST NW", ROUTENAME),
    ROUTENAME = if_else(ROUTENAME == "IRVING ST NE" , "IRVING ST NW", ROUTENAME),
    ROUTENAME = if_else(ROUTENAME == "PARK PL NW"   , "5TH ST NW"   , ROUTENAME),
    )                                                  |>
  group_by(ROUTENAME, build_year)                      |>
  summarise(
    min_install = min(build_year, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_install = max(build_year, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Has some protected lane segments` = if_else(
      max(!is.na(BIKELANE_PROTECTED) + !is.na(BIKELANE_DUAL_PROTECTED)) == 1,
          1, 0),
    n_segments  = n(),
    .groups = "drop" 
  )                                                    |>
  filter(n_segments >= 8) # >= 6
```

```{r}
plot_leaflet(lines_sf = pbl_unioned, 
             line_labels = c("ROUTENAME", "build_year", "Has some protected lane segments"))
```


Note that the categorization of the bike lane types is a little unintuitive. The 17th St NW bike lane, for example, is classified as "buffered" not "protected," which sounds less safe, but the actual bike lane is great:

![The 17th St NW bike lane.](https://www.popville.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/17th-street-bike-lanes-popville.jpg)

(Photo by [Martha Wilson for PopVille](https://www.popville.com/2021/11/bike-lanes-dc-17th-street-nw/))

This bike lane was associated with some of the biggest safety improvements (see below). 

But to be consistent, I've separated the data below according to whether the Open Data DC data set calls the bike lane "protected" or "buffered."

The blue shading below shows the "before" period. The red shading shows the "after" period. I ignore peak COVID years (2020-2023) when calculating the before/after change, since those years were atypical.

Couple high-level findings:

* Overall crashes, driver crashes, and people hitting pedestrians all almost universally go down, often by a lot.
* Bike crashes also often go down, but sometimes they go up. This is likely due to the fact that many more people are biking in those new bike lanes. Even an increase in the raw number of bike crashes in the corridor could mean an actual reduction in the number of crashes _per bike trip_ if way more people are biking on that street because the new bike lane makes it safer. This is almost certainly part of what's happening here.
* The specifics of the projects obviously matter. The 17th St NW street redesign made that street way safer. Contrast that with [Mt Olivet Rd NE](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Mt+Olivet+Rd+NE,+Washington,+DC+20002/@38.9102078,-76.9848517,3a,75y,145.73h,95.83t/data=!3m7!1e1!3m5!1s6eZtSW7cOrx3J2AgdnMpLA!2e0!6shttps:%2F%2Fstreetviewpixels-pa.googleapis.com%2Fv1%2Fthumbnail%3Fcb_client%3Dmaps_sv.tactile%26w%3D900%26h%3D600%26pitch%3D-5.833926890479461%26panoid%3D6eZtSW7cOrx3J2AgdnMpLA%26yaw%3D145.7320796512975!7i16384!8i8192!4m15!1m8!3m7!1s0x89b7b86d6878234f:0xaa6675298b3da622!2sMt+Olivet+Rd+NE,+Washington,+DC+20002!3b1!8m2!3d38.9102445!4d-76.9850932!16s%2Fg%2F1v2yzrly!3m5!1s0x89b7b86d6878234f:0xaa6675298b3da622!8m2!3d38.9102445!4d-76.9850932!16s%2Fg%2F1v2yzrly?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI2MDUyMC4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D), which is still fairly wide (when you include the middle turn lane) and lacking in trees, both of which make drivers go faster.

```{r}

crashes_near_projects <- get_crashes_in_corridors(line_sf = pbl_unioned, crashes_sf = cd, buffer_in_meters = 4)
crashes_near_projects$route_unique_id <- paste(crashes_near_projects$ROUTENAME, crashes_near_projects$max_install)


cd_in_projs_summed <- 
  group_corridor_crashes_by_month(df = crashes_near_projects, 
                                  group_by_vars = c("route_unique_id", "min_install", "max_install", "month", "year", "date", "Has some protected lane segments"),
                                  outcome_vars = outcome_vars)

already_shown <- c("21ST ST NW 2022", "9TH ST NW 2023", "G ST NW 2020",  "MINNESOTA AVE SE 2023", "PENNSYLVANIA AVE SE 2023",  "VIRGINIA AVE NW 2022")
```



## {.tabset}

```{r results="asis"}
for (proj in unique(cd_in_projs_summed$route_unique_id)) {  
  
  temp_df <- filter(cd_in_projs_summed, year >= 2016 & route_unique_id == proj)
  
  proj_year <- unique(temp_df$min_install)
  if(proj_year < 2017) {next}
  is_pbl = temp_df$`Has some protected lane segments`[1]==1
  if(!is_pbl) {next}
  if (temp_df$route_unique_id[1] %in% already_shown) {next}
  
  pbl_flag <- ifelse(is_pbl, " (PBL)", "")
  
  cat("\n### ", proj, pbl_flag, "\n") # tab headers
  
  if (proj_year < 2020) {
    p1sy = 2016; p1ey = proj_year - 1; p2sy = 2024; p2ey = 2025
  } else if (proj_year == 2024) {
    p1sy = 2017; p1ey = 2019; p2sy = 2025; p2ey = 2025
  } else {
    p1sy = 2017; p1ey = 2019; p2sy = 2024; p2ey = 2025
  }
    
  p1      <- list(label = "Pre" ,  start = paste0(2017, "-01-01"), end = paste0(2019, "-12-31"))
  p2      <- list(label = "Post",  start = paste0(2024, "-01-01"), end = paste0(2025, "-12-31"))
  
  rvs <- plot_crashes_over_time(
    data             = temp_df,      
    smoothing_factor = 4,
    period_1         = p1,
    period_2         = p2,
    title            = paste(proj, pbl_flag)
  )
  
  print(rvs[[1]])
  cat("\n")
  print(
    rvs[[3]] %>% 
      rename(Outcome = series,
             `Before, per month` = Pre_per_month,
             `After, per month`  = Post_per_month,
             `% change`          = pct_change) %>%
      knitr::kable()
    )
  
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

## Comparing streets with these new projects against other DC streets

This is all fine and good. But maybe the decline in crashes was not particular to these corridors, and in fact happened across DC during this time? Maybe it's all the new speed cameras, or the fact DC is towing chronic speeders?

To try and answer that question, let's compare these streets with new bike lane projects to other streets in DC, and see if they have similar or different crash trends.










```{r, eval=F}
# source the R script in which we load all of the data:
source("prepare_timeseries.R")

plot_vars <- c(
  "crashes_per_acre",
  
  "injury_crashes_per_acre",
  "driver_injury_crashes_per_acre",
  # "serious_driver_injury_crashes_per_acre",
  
  "bike_injury_crashes_per_acre",
  # "serious_bike_injury_crashes_per_acre",
  
  "ped_injury_crashes_per_acre"
  # "serious_ped_injury_crashes_per_acre"
)

group_types <- c("switcher", "never_taker", "late_taker", "always_taker")

# Nicer labels for facet strip text
var_labels <- c(
  "crashes_per_acre"                      = "All Crashes",
  "injury_crashes_per_acre"               = "Injury Crashes",
  "driver_injury_crashes_per_acre"        = "Driver Injury Crashes",
  # "serious_driver_injury_crashes_per_acre"= "Serious Driver Injury Crashes",
  "bike_injury_crashes_per_acre"          = "Bike Injury Crashes",
  # "serious_bike_injury_crashes_per_acre"  = "Serious Bike Injury Crashes",
  "ped_injury_crashes_per_acre"           = "Ped Injury Crashes"
  # "serious_ped_injury_crashes_per_acre"   = "Serious Ped Injury Crashes"
)

group_labels <- c(
  "switcher"     = "Switchers (PBL installed 2020–2023)",
  "never_taker"  = "Never Takers (no PBL)",
  "late_taker"   = "Late Takers (PBL installed 2024–2025)",
  "always_taker" = "Always Takers (PBL installed before 2019)"
)


# clean the data:
res <- prepare_timeseries()
cd_pbl_clean_simplified <- res[[1]]

# descriptive histograms

# density_plots        <- map(set_names(group_types), \(g) make_density_plots(cd_pbl_clean_simplified, g))
# density_plots_log    <- map(set_names(group_types), \(g) make_density_plots(cd_pbl_clean_simplified, g, log_transform = TRUE))
```

```{r, fig.width=12, eval=F}
run_regs <- function(df, outcome, include_year=T, return_mod=F) {
  print(paste("############### ", outcome))
  print("################################")
  root_reg <- paste0(outcome, " ~ treatment + post_install + treatment*post_install")
  print(summary(lm(formula = as.formula(root_reg), data = df)))
  cat("\n****************************************************")
  print(summary(lm(formula = as.formula(paste0(root_reg, " + mean_crashes_pre2019")), data = df)))
  cat("\n****************************************************")
  print(summary(lm(formula = as.formula(paste0(root_reg, " + mean_crashes_pre2019", 
        ifelse(include_year, " + as.factor(year)", ""))), data = df)))
  cat("\n****************************************************")
  full_mod <- lm(formula = as.formula(
    paste0(root_reg, " + mean_crashes_pre2019 + TOTALTRAVELLANEWIDTH + TOTALPARKINGLANES ",
          "+ as.factor(WARD_ID) + as.factor(DCFUNCTIONALCLASS) + total_change_trips + cabi_rides",
           ifelse(include_year, " + as.factor(year)", ""))),
    data = df)
  print(summary(full_mod))

  if (return_mod) {
    return(full_mod)
  }
}
```

```{r, eval=F}
run_regs <- function(df, outcome, include_year = TRUE) {
  root_reg <- paste0(outcome, " ~ treatment + post_install + treatment*post_install")
  year_term <- ifelse(include_year, " + as.factor(year)", "")

  formulas <- list(
    simple = as.formula(root_reg),
    full   = as.formula(paste0(
      root_reg,
      " + mean_crashes_pre2019 + TOTALTRAVELLANEWIDTH + TOTALPARKINGLANES",
      " + as.factor(WARD_ID) + as.factor(DCFUNCTIONALCLASS) + total_change_trips",
      year_term
    ))
  )

  map_dfr(formulas, \(f) {
    tidy(lm(f, data = df)) |>
      filter(term == "treatment:post_install") |>
      mutate(outcome = outcome)
  }, .id = "model")
}


plot_effects <- function(outcomes, df) {
  results <- map_dfr(outcomes, \(o) {
    run_regs(df = df, outcome = o, include_year = FALSE)
  })
  
  results <- results |>
    mutate(significance = case_when(
        p.value < 0.001 ~ "p < 0.001",
        p.value < 0.01  ~ "p < 0.01",
        p.value < 0.05  ~ "p < 0.05",
        p.value < 0.10  ~ "p < 0.10",
        TRUE            ~ "p ≥ 0.10"
      ),
      significance = factor(significance,
                            levels = c("p < 0.001", "p < 0.01",
                                       "p < 0.05", "p < 0.10",  "p ≥ 0.10")),
      model  = factor(model, levels = c("simple", "full"),
                      labels = c("Simple model", "Full model")),
      outcome = factor(outcome, levels = outcomes) |> # preserve ordering
        fct_relabel(\(x) str_replace_all(x, "_", " ") |>
                                str_replace(" per acre", "") |>
                                str_to_sentence())
    )
  
  sig_colors <- c(
    "p < 0.001"       = "#2166ac",
    "p < 0.01"        = "#74add1",
    "p < 0.05"        = "#fdae61",
    "p < 0.10"        = "#fee08b",
    "p ≥ 0.10"        = "#d9d9d9"
  )
  
  ggplot(
          results,
         # filter(results, model=="Simple model"), 
         aes(x = outcome, y = estimate, fill = significance)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.6) +
    geom_errorbar(
      aes(ymin = estimate - 1.645 * std.error,
          ymax = estimate + 1.645 * std.error),
      position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
      width = 0.2, color = "grey30"
    ) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = sig_colors, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = \(x) str_replace_all(x, "_", "\n")) +
    facet_wrap(~model, ncol=1) +
    labs(
      title = "Effect of protected bike lane installation on crash outcomes",
      subtitle = "Coefficient on treatment × post-install interaction",
      x     = NULL,
      y     = "Estimated effect per acre",
      fill  = "Significance"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x     = element_text(size = 8),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
    )
}


plot_effects(
  outcomes = c(
      "crashes_per_acre",
      "injury_crashes_per_acre",
      
      "driver_injury_crashes_per_acre",
      "serious_driver_injury_crashes_per_acre",
  
      "bike_injury_crashes_per_acre",
      "serious_bike_injury_crashes_per_acre",
      
      "ped_injury_crashes_per_acre",
      "serious_ped_injury_crashes_per_acre"
      ),
  df = filter(cd_pbl_clean_simplified, (switcher == 1) | (never_taker == 1) | (late_taker == 1))  
  )
```

```{r, eval=F}
summary_df <-
  cd_pbl_clean_simplified |>
  filter(switcher == 1 | never_taker == 1) |>
  select(!!!sym(ANALYSIS_LEVEL), post_install, treatment, ends_with("_per_acre")) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(outcomes),
               names_to  = "outcome",
               values_to = "value") |>
  group_by(outcome, post_install, treatment) |>        # add treatment to grouping
  summarise(
    mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    post_install = factor(post_install, levels = c(0, 1),
                          labels = c("Pre", "Post")),
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = c(0, 1),
                       labels = c("Other streets", "PBL installs")),
    outcome = factor(outcome, levels = outcomes) |>
                fct_relabel(\(x) str_replace_all(x, "_", " ") |>
                              str_replace(" per acre", "") |>
                              str_to_sentence())
  )

ggplot(summary_df, aes(x = post_install, y = mean,
                       color = treatment, group = treatment)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~outcome, nrow = 1,
             labeller = labeller(outcome = label_wrap_gen(15))) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Other streets"   = "grey50",
                                "PBL installs" = "#4575b4")) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean annual crashes per acre before and after bike lane installation",
    x     = NULL,
    y     = "Crashes per acre",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position    = "bottom",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    strip.text         = element_text(size = 7)
  )
```
